label: GO after an unrewarded rare a2 trial (stay on a2), late in episode
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2), only when the previous trial was unrewarded (in_rew=0), and almost only when the previous trial was a2 with a rare transition to S1 (rare-unrewarded a2: the model-based response is to stay on a2). The policy at these steps strongly favors a2 (choice logit < -5; 94% of mass is in the bottom choice bin, model_act=a2 for nearly all activations). It is essentially silent before episode trial ~55 and is strongest in trials 60-90, so it is gated by time in the episode. On a window first trial (rel -3) the previous trial is outside the window, so prev_common/prev_action unknown (-1) are allowed; those steps make up about 19% of mass. Uses only observed variables plus the agent own policy. It does NOT fire after rewarded trials, after a1 choices, or after common unrewarded a2 trials (prev_common=1 has 0.1x lift). Without the choice condition F1 drops to ~0.75 (precision 0.63), so magnitude and occurrence also depend on how strongly the agent is committed to a2. Magnitude was not checked beyond the quartile coverage, which is roughly flat across the conditions.

issues: The label holds up. The feature fires only at GO (D1 and D2 have 0 activations). It needs prev_reward=0 (prev_reward=1 gives 21 of 14660 actives). It needs the previous trial to be a2 that reached S1 by a rare transition: after a common unrewarded a2 trial the predicate's precision is 0.002. It is silent before about trial 50: with the core condition, precision is 0.011 for ep_trial 40-54, 0.23 for 55-59 and about 0.89 for 60 and later.

The explanation is wrong about the choice condition. When the previous trial is in the window, choice<-5 adds almost nothing: for prev_action=2 & prev_state=1 & prev_reward=0 & ep_trial>=60, precision is 0.885 without it and 0.888 with it. The choice condition only matters on the window's first trial (rel -3), where prev_action and prev_common are unknown. So the precision drop to 0.63 without choice comes from that window-boundary slice, not from the policy's commitment to a2 in general.

There is a systematic false-positive class at rel -3. The slice GO & prev_reward=0 & rel=-3 & ep_trial>=60 & choice<-5 has precision 0.59 (4248 predicted). Most of the 3095 dev false positives are rel -3 GO steps where, as far as one can tell, the unseen previous trial was a common a2 trial to S2. Tightening that slice to choice<-9 raises its precision to 0.94 while keeping most of its recall (0.159 vs 0.171).

There is a small miss class: GO after an unrewarded common a1 trial (also in S1), when the agent switches to a2 with choice<-5. Precision there is 0.58 but recall is only about 2%. With the rest of the scattered misses this is 3.4% of dev mass and 3.8% of test mass, which is minor. Together with the prev_state analysis, it suggests the feature is mainly about an unrewarded visit to S1 combined with a strong pull toward a2. 'Rare a2' covers almost all of it, because the agent rarely chooses a1 at these steps.

Better predicate (observed variables only): treat the previous trial explicitly as a2 to S1 when it is known, and use a stricter choice threshold at rel -3. Its dev F1 is 0.890 and test F1 is 0.891 (precision 0.904, recall 0.877, mass recall 0.953), against the reported test F1 of 0.844.
